{{Nihongo|'''Kushida-jinja'''|櫛田神社}} is a [[Shinto]] {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|en|Hakata-ku, Fukuoka|qid=Q1330839|lt=Hakata-ku, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}. Dedicated to [[Amaterasu]] and [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]], it is said to have been founded in 757. The {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qid=Q1749262|lt=Hakata Gion Yamakasa}} [[Japanese festivals|festival]] is centred on the shrine.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/showcase/english/theme/db_object_37.html |title=Kushida Shrine |publisher={{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}} |accessdate=24 March 2011}}</ref>

==Overview==

'''Kushida Shrine''' (くしだじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Kamikawabatamachi, [[:en:Hakata-ku|Hakata-ku]], [[:en:Fukuoka City|Fukuoka City]], {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}}. The former [[shrine Rank]] was [[Prefectural Shrine]]. It is situated in the old town area of Hakata and is affectionately known by locals as "'''Okushida-san'''." Its formal name is '''Hakata Sōchinshu Kushida Shrine''' (はかたそうちんじゅくしだじんじゃ).

== Overview ==
The shrine has long been revered as the [[Ujigami]] and general {{ill|Chinjusha|en|Chinjusha|qid=Q13479654|lt=Chinjusha}} (guardian deity) of Hakata. It hosts festivals such as the {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|en|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|qid=Q1749262|lt=Hakata Gion Yamakasa}} in July and the [[Hakata Okunchi]] in October. Although the [[Hakata Matsubayashi]] (Hakata Dontaku) in May is not strictly a Kushida Shrine festival, the Matsubayashi procession traditionally starts from Kushida Shrine<ref>{{Cite book|author=Kiyoshi Tanaka, Osamu Matsuda, Noriko Obayashi, Takashi Tomokiyo |title=Hakata Tabijō: Shiki no Gyoji Rekishi Yomoyama |publisher=Eizo Yagi |date=1967-04-25 |page=88}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|author=Seizo Inoue |title=Hakata Kyōdo Shi Jiten |publisher=Sanda Hisamoto |date=1987-11-01 |pages=264-266}}</ref>.

== festival Deities ==
The shrine enshrines three deities: [[Ōhata-nushi no Ōkami]] (Kushida no Ōkami), [[Amaterasu]], and [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo no Ōkami]] (Gion no Ōkami). The main hall enshrines Ōhata-nushi no Ōkami, the left hall enshrines Amaterasu Ōmikami, and the right hall enshrines Susanoo no Ōkami.

Unlike other Kushida Shrines across Japan that mainly enshrine [[Kushinadahime]], Kushinadahime is not enshrined here, although there is a theory that this shrine originally enshrined her.

Ōhata-nushi no Ōkami (Kushida no Ōkami) is believed to be a deity transferred from {{ill|Kushida|en|Kushida |qid=Q1794549|lt=Kushida Shrine in Matsusaka}}, {{ill|Ise Province|en|Ise Province|qid=Q864166|lt=Ise Province}}. Also known as Ōwakako no Mikoto, he is a descendant of [[Ame-no-Minakanushi]] and is said to have vanquished monsters in the Hokuriku region. There is a shrine dedicated to Ōhata-nushi no Ōkami in [[Sado City]], and among the five shrines dedicated to Kushinadahime, three are located in the Hokuriku region.

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, Kushida Shrine was established in {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|en|Tenpyō-hōji|qid=Q1346307|lt=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 (757) when the deity from {{ill|Kushida|en|Kushida |qid=Q1794549|lt=Kushida Shrine in Matsusaka}} was transferred here, along with Amaterasu Ōmikami, who served the clan of Ōhata-nushi no Ōkami, the deity of the Matsusaka shrine. In {{ill|Tengyō|en|Tengyō|qid=Q1327340|lt=Tengyō}} 4 (941), Ono no Yoshifuru prayed at [[Yasaka Shrine]] in Kyoto to suppress the [[Rebellion of Fujiwara no Sumitomo]] and subsequently transferred Susanoo no Ōkami to this shrine after pacifying the rebellion. However, the most widely accepted theory is that in the late Heian period, [[Taira no Kiyomori]] transferred [[Kushida Shrine (Saga)|Kushida Shrine]] in {{ill|Kanzaki|en|Kanzaki|qid=Q1728232|lt=Kanzaki}}, {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|qid=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}} (now Kanzaki City, Saga Prefecture) to Hakata, a base for Japan-Song trade. This theory is supported by the 'Hakata Yamakasa Record' compiled by the shrine priests and submitted to the Ministry of Education in {{ill|1965|en|1965|qid=Q2650|lt=1965}} and 'The History of Fukuoka' published by Fukuoka City in {{ill|1979|en|1979|qid=Q2484|lt=1979}}, both of which indicate the shrine is a branch of Kushida Shrine in Kanzaki, Saga Prefecture.

The shrine fell into decline during the {{ill|Sengoku period|en|Sengoku period|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}},<ref>'The location of Kushida Shrine in Hakata seems to have been given to the Jesuits by [[:en:Ōtomo Yoshishige|Ōtomo Yoshishige]], who built a church and a priest's residence there. According to 'History of the Jesuits in Japan' (Vol. 10, Western Kyushu Part 2, pp. 27-31, published September 20, 1979, translated by Kiichi Matsuda and Taro Kawasaki, Chūōkōronsha), there was a dispute between the Jesuits and the people of Hakata regarding the storage of tools used for the Hakata Gion Yamakasa festival.' </ref> but in {{ill|1587|en|1587|qid=Q6744|lt=1587}} (Tensho 15), {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} rebuilt the shrine during the reconstruction of Hakata.

Before the [[Shinbutsu bunri]] decree in {{ill|1868|en|1868|qid=Q7717|lt=1868}} (Meiji 1), the shrine was managed by {{ill|Jingū-ji|en|Jingū-ji|qid=Q1074971|lt=Jingū-ji}} belonging to {{ill|Tōchō-ji|en|Tōchō-ji|qid=Q3547067|lt=Tōchō-ji}} during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}.

In {{ill|1891|en|1891|qid=Q7837|lt=1891}} (Meiji 24), it was listed as a [[Prefectural Shrine]].

== Miscellaneous ==
The name of [[Gionmachi]] in [[:en:Hakata-ku|Hakata-ku]], [[:en:Fukuoka City|Fukuoka City]], is said to derive from Gion no Ōkami enshrined at this shrine<ref name="reizen">[http://www.asocie.jp/reizen/profile/record/oldtown1.html History of Reizen District 1945-2007, Reizen District Union]</ref>.

A decorated Yamakasa float is permanently displayed in the precincts. Since {{ill|1960|en|1960|qid=Q3754|lt=1960}} (Showa 35), {{ill|Kyushu Asahi Broadcasting|en|Kyushu Asahi Broadcasting|qid=Q843686|lt=Kyushu Asahi Broadcasting}} (KBC) has been airing 'Hashire! Yamakasa' as an offering.

In addition, near the entrance of the precincts stands a 1,000-year-old ginkgo tree called "Kushida no Ginnan," which is mentioned in the '[[Hakata Iwaiuta]]' and is designated a natural monument of the prefecture.

The "Cut-Tree Peony,"<ref>'[https://web.archive.org/web/20210419114128/https://www.city.karatsu.lg.jp/manabee/kyoiku/kyoiku/inkai/bunkazai/bunkazaihogo/kirigonobotan.html Prefectural Natural Monument Cut-Tree Peony]'. Karatsu City. Archived from the original on April 19, 2021. </ref> associated with [[Hata no Chikahira|Hata no Mikawa no Kami Chikahira]] of the [[Matsuura Clan]], whose peonies decorate the Yamakasa, was transplanted from Hizen Town, Karatsu City, in {{ill|2018|en|2018|qid=Q25291|lt=2018}} (Heisei 30)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hakata Gion Yamakasa and Peony Connection - Kushida Shrine in Fukuoka Receives Peony from Karatsu|url=https://www.saga-s.co.jp/articles/-/308161|website=Saga Newspaper LiVE|accessdate=2019-12-02|language=ja}}</ref>.

In {{ill|1955|en|1955|qid=Q18577|lt=1955}} (Showa 30), Typhoon No. 22 caused damage such as toppling an [[:en:Enoki|Enoki]] tree in the precincts<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kushida Shrine - Fallen Enoki Tree - Nishinippon Photo Library|url=http://c.nishinippon.co.jp/photolibrary/cat672/post_1691.php|website=c.nishinippon.co.jp|accessdate=2020-04-08|language=ja}}</ref>.
